current_example.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- If an integer $n$ is even, then there exists an integer $p$ such that $n=2p.$

- If an integer $n$ is odd, then there exists an integer $q$ such that $n=2q+1.$

In this case, we need to prove the following:

$$
4n^2+5n-1 \text{ is odd}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
n \text{ is even}
$$

To prove $P \Rightarrow Q,$ it suffices to prove the contrapositive $\neg Q \Rightarrow \neg P.$

The contrapositive form of the given statement is

$$
n \text{ is not even}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
4n^2+5n-1 \text{ is not odd}
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}n \text{ is odd}}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}4n^2+5n-1 \text{ is even}}.
$$

We start by using the fact that $n$ is odd.

If $n$ is $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{odd}},$ then
$n = \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2a+1},$
where $a$ is $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{an integer}}.$

The idea is to substitute $n=2a+1$ into the expression $4n^2+5n-1$ and show it is even by writing it as a multiple of $2.$

Substituting ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14274149/assets/0f6749abbc48ba10ef22aea628f4ccdc3b297376f751f2b7a8c22d623a893c33.svg) into the expression $4n^2+5n-1,$ we can show that $4n^2+5n-1 = \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2b},$ where $b$ is $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{an integer}}.$

Once we've done this, the proof is complete, and we can state our conclusion.

Therefore, since $4n^2+5n-1$ $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{is}}$ a multiple of $2,$ we conclude that $4n^2+5n-1$ is $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{even}}.$
